---
title: "Wide figures in galleries (R)"
format:
  html:
    code-tools: true
filters:
  - panzoom
panzoom:
  hint: false
---

Collages (25 × 2 inches) and tall strips in galleries, as subfigures, and in a
layout div. The same shapes on their own, and the `fit` option, are on [wide and
tall figures](h-wide-and-tall-r.html).

Wide figures open at screen height, and tall ones at screen width. The one you
click opens at the spot you clicked, and stepping to another in a gallery starts
it at its left end or top. In a gallery, the left and right arrow keys pan a
wide figure, and at its end one more press moves to the next image; holding the
key down stops at the end. On a tall strip they do nothing. The previous and
next buttons step through the gallery. The viewer keeps the sides of the screen
free for them, so a figure shown whole, or panned to its end, is never under a
button.

The plots are drawn with these helpers:

```{r}
# A collage: `n` panels side by side, like a wide patchwork figure.
collage <- function(n = 12) {
  set.seed(1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, n), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(
      cumsum(rnorm(200)),
      type = "l",
      main = paste("Panel", i),
      xlab = "",
      ylab = "",
      col = hcl.colors(n)[i],
      lwd = 2
    )
  }
}

# A tall strip: `n` rows stacked, like a tall patchwork figure.
# Each seed gets its own palette (without its lightest end), so different
# strips look different.
strip <- function(seed = 2, n = 8) {
  set.seed(seed)
  palette <- c(
    "Viridis",
    "Plasma",
    "Zissou 1",
    "Dark 3",
    "Sunset",
    "Cividis",
    "Dynamic",
    "Inferno"
  )[(seed - 2) %% 8 + 1]
  par(mfrow = c(n, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(
      cumsum(rnorm(100)),
      type = "l",
      main = paste0("Strip ", seed, ", row ", i),
      xlab = "",
      ylab = "",
      col = hcl.colors(n + 2, palette)[i],
      lwd = 2
    )
  }
}
```

## Gallery of two collages {expect-fit="height"}

Two 25 × 2 inch collages in a gallery. Each opens at screen height. The left and
right arrow keys and dragging pan along the collage, and at its end one more
press moves to the other collage, as do the previous and next buttons.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: collages
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-alt:
#|   - >-
#|     A row of 12 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#|   - >-
#|     A row of 15 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "A 25 × 2 inch collage of 12 random walks."
#|   - "A 25 × 2 inch collage of 15 random walks."

collage(n = 12)
collage(n = 15)
```

## Gallery of two tall strips {expect-fit="width"}

Two tall strips in a gallery. Each opens at screen width and extends downwards.
The left and right arrow keys do nothing, since there is nowhere to go sideways,
and the previous and next buttons move between the strips.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: strips
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "A column of 8 small line plots of random walks"
#|   - "A column of 8 small line plots of random walks"
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "A 4 × 15 inch strip of 8 random walks."
#|   - "A 4 × 15 inch strip of 8 more random walks."

strip(seed = 8, n = 8)
strip(seed = 9, n = 8)
```

## Stacked collages {expect-fit="height"}

Two collages stacked as subfigures. Each opens at screen height, and the two
form a gallery.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| label: fig-collage-rows
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| layout-nrow: 2
#| fig-alt:
#|   - >-
#|     A row of 12 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#|   - >-
#|     A row of 15 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| fig-cap: "Collages of 12 and 15 random walks, stacked."
#| fig-subcap: ["First collage", "Second collage"]

collage(n = 12)
collage(n = 15)
```

## Strips side by side {expect-fit="width"}

Two tall strips side by side as subfigures. Each opens at screen width, and the
two form a gallery.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| label: fig-strip-cols
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "A column of 8 small line plots of random walks"
#|   - "A column of 8 small line plots of random walks"
#| fig-cap: "Two 4 × 15 inch strips of 8 random walks, side by side."
#| fig-subcap: ["First strip", "Second strip"]

strip(seed = 2, n = 8)
strip(seed = 3, n = 8)
```

## Tall strips in a layout div {expect-fit="width"}

Two code cells in a `.panzoom` div with a layout. Each strip opens at screen
width on its own, with no gallery, since they aren't subfigures.

````markdown {.code-overflow-wrap .cell-code}
::: {.panzoom layout-ncol="2"}
```{{r}}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-alt: "A column of 8 small line plots of random walks"

strip(seed = 4, n = 8)
```

```{{r}}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-alt: "A column of 8 small line plots of random walks"

strip(seed = 5, n = 8)
```
:::
````

::: {.panzoom layout-ncol="2"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-alt: "A column of 8 small line plots of random walks"

strip(seed = 4, n = 8)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-alt: "A column of 8 small line plots of random walks"

strip(seed = 5, n = 8)
```
:::

## Collages of different lengths {expect-fit="height"}

A long collage (40 × 2 in, 24 panels) and a shorter one (24 × 2 in, 12 panels)
from two cells, joined by `group`. Each opens at screen height, and stepping to
the other fits it afresh, from its left end, so the short collage doesn't keep
the scale or position of the long one. Only the short collage has a description,
so the caption band changes height between them, and each collage stays clear of
it. `fig-dpi: 48` only keeps the files small.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: mixed-collages
#| fig-width: 40
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-dpi: 48
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A row of 24 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| fig-cap: "A 40 × 2 inch collage of 24 random walks."

collage(n = 24)
```

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: mixed-collages
#|   description: >-
#|     Each panel is a random walk of 200 steps, colored along a single palette
#|     from the first panel to the last, and titled with its panel number so the
#|     order can be read at any zoom.
#| fig-width: 24
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-dpi: 48
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A row of 12 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| fig-cap: "A 24 × 2 inch collage of 12 random walks."

collage(n = 12)
```

## Strips of different lengths {expect-fit="width"}

Strips of different sizes, 4 × 20 in (10 rows) and 3 × 12 in (6 rows), in a
layout div with captions of different lengths. Each opens at screen width from
its top, on its own, and the layout shows them at different heights on the page.

````markdown {.code-overflow-wrap .cell-code}
::: {.panzoom layout-ncol="2"}
```{{r}}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 20
#| fig-alt: "A column of 10 small line plots of random walks"
#| fig-cap: "A 4 × 20 inch strip of 10 random walks."

strip(seed = 6, n = 10)
```

```{{r}}
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-alt: "A column of 6 small line plots of random walks"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   A 3 × 12 inch strip of 6 random walks of 100 steps each, stacked in one
#|   column, each row in its own color.

strip(seed = 7, n = 6)
```
:::
````

::: {.panzoom layout-ncol="2"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 20
#| fig-alt: "A column of 10 small line plots of random walks"
#| fig-cap: "A 4 × 20 inch strip of 10 random walks."

strip(seed = 6, n = 10)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-alt: "A column of 6 small line plots of random walks"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   A 3 × 12 inch strip of 6 random walks of 100 steps each, stacked in one
#|   column, each row in its own color.

strip(seed = 7, n = 6)
```
:::

## Collages in a custom layout {expect-fit="height" expect-steps="true"}

Three collages as subfigures with `layout: [[1, 1], [1]]`: two side by side, and
one across the row below. Each opens at screen height, and the three form a
gallery in reading order.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| label: fig-collage-layout
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| layout: [[1, 1], [1]]
#| fig-alt:
#|   - >-
#|     A row of 12 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#|   - >-
#|     A row of 15 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#|   - >-
#|     A row of 9 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| fig-cap: "Collages of 12, 15, and 9 random walks."
#| fig-subcap: ["First collage", "Second collage", "Third collage"]

collage(n = 12)
collage(n = 15)
collage(n = 9)
```

## Collages in a layout with a gap {expect-fit="height" expect-steps="true"}

Three collages as subfigures with `layout: [[45, -10, 45], [100]]`: two at 45%
of the width with an empty 10% between them, and one across the row below. The
gap is an empty cell, not an image, so the three still form a gallery in reading
order.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| label: fig-collage-gap
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| layout: [[45, -10, 45], [100]]
#| fig-alt:
#|   - >-
#|     A row of 12 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#|   - >-
#|     A row of 15 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#|   - >-
#|     A row of 9 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| fig-cap: "Collages of 12, 15, and 9 random walks."
#| fig-subcap: ["First collage", "Second collage", "Third collage"]

collage(n = 12)
collage(n = 15)
collage(n = 9)
```
